_about: The ONE positioning source of FileDO (SITE-REPRESENTATION rules 1 and 2, SP-0157). Every external surface that lists what the product does - the landing and its two standalone locale pages, the guides hub, the five READMEs, the Store listing source, the winget manifest - is written from this list and names the pillars in this order; a surface too short for all of them names the first ones. No surface is written from another surface; where two disagree this file decides which is wrong. Read by packaging/check-external-docs.ps1, step 'positioning'. Each 'surfaces' entry names a file, the region of it that lists the pillars ('scopes', regular expressions, one region each) and, per pillar, a regular expression that finds that pillar's words in that file's language. The step fails when a region is not found, when a pillar the surface must name (the first 'names' pillars, less 'allowMissing') is not found in a region, or when the last word of one pillar comes after the first word of the next. A change of the order is a change of this file first, then of every surface.
lead: Know your storage before you trust it.
tagline: Test USB sticks and SD cards for fake capacity

localized._about: The lead and the tagline as the READMEs word them in the other languages (SP-0166 P4). The English pair is 'lead' and 'tagline' above: the lead is the promise (the H1 of every README, 'FileDO - <lead>'), the tagline is the category phrase under it (the opening of the italic summary of README.md, README.ru.md and README.ua.md, and of the winget ShortDescription). Step 'lead' of packaging/check-external-docs.ps1 compares letters and digits only, case ignored. A wording change is a change of this file first, then of every surface that carries it; the translations are still read against the English by step 'locales'.

pillars.title: Check
pillars.says: The real capacity (fake-capacity detection), the speed and the readability of a drive, folder or network share.

pillars.title: Tidy and move
pillars.says: Find duplicates, compare two folders, copy large trees with progress and care for slow or damaged disks.

pillars.title: Erase
pillars.says: Wipe free space and single files by overwriting them, to make recovery harder, and empty folders (a plain delete) - a file or folder wipe asks for a typed confirmation unless you pass --yes.

pillars.title: Protect
pillars.says: Pack a file or a folder into a password-protected .fd-sec container and open it again.

pillars.title: Virtual disks
pillars.says: A whole volume in one .fdd file, mounted as a drive letter or read without mounting.

tagDenyList._about: Words that must never appear in a tag or a search term the build owns (SP-0166 P4, PROMOTION section 4 item 5): the Tags of every winget locale manifest, every @@SearchTerm of msix/listing/*.txt, and the tags of a Scoop manifest or a Chocolatey nuspec the caller names on the command line. Owned by the feature-to-site flow: a word is added when a channel's tag would over-claim or contradict a decision. A competitor's name is NEVER added - this file is tracked and public, so listing a name here would publish it. An entry denies every tag word that starts with it; case is ignored and a hyphen, an underscore or a space count as one separator, so 'file-manager' and 'file manager' are the same entry. 'words' applies to the tags and search terms of every locale, 'locale' adds to the words of its own language (ru, ua, de, fr; the Store file uk.txt is ua). The docs/termbase.json 'forbidden' fragments are held against the same fields by the same step and are not repeated here. Read by packaging/check-external-docs.ps1, step 'tags'.

words.encryption: A .fd-sec or .fdd without a password is obfuscated, not encrypted, so FileDO is not listed as encryption software (docs/termbase.json term 'obfuscation').
words.encrypt: The same claim as a verb or a participle (encrypts, encrypted).
words.file-manager: The Store category stays 'Utilities + tools' / 'Backup + manage', never 'File managers' (msix/store-listing.md); FileDO is a storage tool, not a file manager.
words.file manager: The same, written with a space.
words.secure-eras: A wipe makes recovery harder and promises nothing on an SSD, so 'secure' over-claims.
words.data-wip: The same over-claim; the tag for the feature is 'wipe'.
words.md5: The duplicate finder hashes with SHA-256, not MD5.
words.alternative: No tag or search term of the form 'X alternative': a competitor is never named or implied (PROMOTION section 1 rule 4).
words.filemanager: The same, written as one word.
words.file manag: The same, for 'file-management' (it reads as a file manager).

claimDenyList._about: Wording the descriptions must never carry (SP-0166 P4, the over-claim traps of the promotion campaign): the winget ShortDescription and Description of every locale manifest, the Store @@ShortDescription of every locale, and the description, notes, summary and title of a Scoop manifest or a Chocolatey nuspec the caller names on the command line. Each key is a regular expression matched as a whole word, case-insensitive; 'all' applies to every text, a language key adds to the texts of that language (ru, ua, de, fr; the Store file uk.txt is ua). A competitor's name is NEVER added (this file is public). The network entries stand until release-queue row 2 / SP-0065 gives the privacy claim its disk-sharing carve-out; drop them in that change. Read by packaging/check-external-docs.ps1, step 'claims'.

all.#1: A ranking; no source backs one.
all.MD5: The duplicate finder hashes with SHA-256, not MD5.
all.multi[- ]?[KMGT]B\\s*/\\s*s: The multi-GB/s form: no measured artefact in the tree backs a throughput claim.
all.\\d[\\d.,]*\\+?\\s*[KMGT]B\\s*/\\s*s: A throughput figure: a number is read from its source at writing time, and a description has none.
all.\\d[\\d.,]*\\+?\\s*[KMGT]i?B\\s*(?:/|per: A throughput figure in any unit spelling: a number is read from its source at writing time, and a description has none.
all.file[- ]?manager: FileDO is a storage tool, not a file manager; the Store category stays 'Backup + manage' (msix/store-listing.md).
all.encryption\\s+(?:software|tool|app): A .fd-sec or .fdd without a password is obfuscated, not encrypted; FileDO is not encryption software (docs/termbase.json term 'obfuscation').

en.fast(?:er|est)?(?!\\s+media\\s+sorter): 'fast' and 'fastest' are unsourced boasts; FileDO's own verb 'fastcopy' and the sibling product's name 'Fast Media Sorter' are different words and pass.
en.best(?!-effort): A ranking; no source backs one.
en.securely: A wipe makes recovery harder and promises nothing on an SSD.
en.secure[- ]?(?:wip|eras|delet)\\w*: The same over-claim (secure wipe, erase, deletion).
en.DoD: A wipe is never described by a defence standard.
en.(?:un|ir)recoverable: Recovery is made harder, never impossible.
en.quick(?:ly)?\\s+(?:\\w+\\s+)?(?:checks?|: The capacity test fills the free space and is slow on large media, so it is never a quick check.
en.never\\s+(?:connects\\b|connect\\s+to\\b: Disk sharing through Fast Media Sorter exists, so no absolute network claim is made until SP-0065 adds the carve-out.
en.(?:whole|entire)\\s+(?:device|drive|disk: The capacity test covers the free space, not the whole device.
en.every\\s+(?:byte|fake): The read-back is sampled and the verdict can be Not proven, so nothing is checked byte by byte or every time.
en.vault|encrypted\\s+archive: A .fd-sec or .fdd without a password is obfuscated, never a vault or an encrypted archive (docs/termbase.json).
en.recovery\\s+(?:is\\s+)?impossible|imposs: A wipe makes recovery harder, never impossible; a folder wipe is a delete.
en.signed\\s+(?:and\\s+verified\\s+)?(?:ins: The setup is unsigned and SmartScreen warns.
